title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
technique: speculative decoding with feature-level (second-to-top-layer) autoregressive draft head plus tree drafts

optimized_metrics.evidence: EAGLE primarily focuses on latency rather than throughput. We assess acceleration effects using the following metrics: Walltime speedup ratio: The actual test speedup ratio relative to vanilla autoregressive decoding.
while maintaining the distribution of the generated text.

headline_claim.text: For LLaMA2-Chat 70B, EAGLE achieved a latency speedup ratio of 2.7x-3.5x, doubled throughput, while maintaining the distribution of the generated text.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Walltime speedup ratio: The actual test speedup ratio relative to vanilla autoregressive decoding.
metric_definitions.notes: batch size 1 default; relative, not absolute latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Average acceptance length τ : The average number of tokens accepted per forward pass of the target LLM.
Acceptance rate α: The ratio of accepted to generated tokens during drafting, gauges draft accuracy.

load_regime: batch=1 for most experiments; batch size 1-4 (and max batch for throughput) in §4.4; single-prompt benchmark runs (MT-bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca)
tradeoff_acknowledged: speedup ratio diminishes with increasing batch size (3.01x at bs=1 to 2.40x at bs=4 for 70B); slightly more CUDA memory (max bs 8 -> 7)
extractor_notes: Not a serving paper; latency means single-stream decode speed. Throughput is secondary (Section 4.4). Two-column text extraction is interleaved.
